ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
In the field of military technology, a special material with a negative refractive index has been invented. When electromagnetic waves pass through air and this material, the propagation laws of the electromagnetic waves remain unchanged, and the relationship between the angles of incidence and refraction still follows the law of refraction (in this case, the angle of refraction takes a negative value, meaning the angles of refraction and incidence are on the same side of the normal). Now, a cylindrical object made of this material with a semicircular cross-section is placed horizontally on a light-absorbing ground, as shown in the figure. A vertical plane coordinate system is established with the center of the circle as the origin. A monochromatic light beam is incident from the left at the vertex of the semicircle. The speed of light in vacuum is \( c \), and the refractive index of this material for the monochromatic light is \( n = -2 \). The radius of the semicircle is \( R \).

1. By changing the angle of incidence, what is the range of the horizontal coordinate of the light spot on the ground?
2. What is the time range for the monochromatic light to propagate in the material?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a semicircular-section object placed on a horizontal light-absorbing ground. The diameter of the semicircle is on the horizontal ground, and a coordinate origin is established at the center of the circle; the x-axis is along the ground to the right, and the y-axis is vertically upward. The vertex of the semicircle is above the y-axis, corresponding to coordinates (0,R). A beam of monochromatic light is obliquely incident from the upper left to the vertex of the semicircle. Reasoning: Let the angle of incidence be i, with the angle measured relative to the vertical normal at the vertex. Take the refractive index of air as 1, and the refractive index of the material as n=-2. From the law of refraction there is sin i = -2 sin r. Since the refracted angle in a negative-refractive-index material takes a negative value, let φ=|r| represent the angle of the refracted ray inside the material relative to the downward vertical direction; then sin φ = sin i / 2. When changing the angle of incidence, i can vary from 0 to approaching 90°, therefore sin φ varies from 0 to approaching 1/2, that is, φ varies from 0 to approaching 30°, so φ ∈ [0, π/6). According to the geometry in the figure, after the light ray enters the material from the vertex (0,R), it propagates toward the lower left and reaches the ground y=0. The vertical descending distance is R, and the horizontal displacement is -R tan φ, therefore the horizontal coordinate of the light spot is x = -R tan φ. Thus the range of values of x is (-R/√3, 0], that is, (-√3 R/3, 0]. The optical path length inside the material is L = R / cos φ. The magnitude of the light speed in the material is c/|n| = c/2, so the propagation time t = L/(c/2)=2L/c = 2R/(c cos φ). When φ=0, t=2R/c; when φ approaches π/6, t approaches 2R/(c·√3/2)=4√3R/(3c), but the upper end cannot be taken. Therefore the time range is [2R/c, 4√3R/(3c)).
